newsitem.title: POLAND: Statoil eyes 150 outlets in Poland by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Statoil eyes 150 outlets in Poland by 2000.

text.p: Norway's Statoil plans to invest $350 million to $400 million by the year 2000 to lift its number of petrol stations in Poland to 150 from the current 47, Statoil's director general told the daily Rzeczpospolita.
"We figure that by the end of the year 2000 we will pay out $350 million to $400 million for the building of petrol stations," Soren Nielsen told the paper in its Saturday issue.
Nielsen also reiterated his firm's intention to take part in the privatisation of Polish refineries, which would significantly increase the planned investment.
He said Statoil planned its 1997 investment in Poland to reach $150 million and for 60-65 stations to be in place then.
Nielsen also said his firm sought to sell products such as natural gas and heating oil in Poland.
A recent report by the private Polish Liquid Fuels Chamber showed that Poland had 5,234 petrol stations in January this year, of which 26 percent belonged to state-owned network CPN.

CPN owned 1,367 stations while state-owned refineries Petrochemia Plock SA and Rafineria Gdansk SA, two firms to be partially sold off next year under the government's oil sector privatisation scheme, controlled 190 and 79 respectively.
The privatisation plan also provides for giving investors in the refineries access to CPN's chain and some 13 foreign firms have showed interest.
The Fuels Chamber report said Statoil was the fourth biggest fuel retailer in Poland.
